items.label: A
items.critique: Lively and plain, but all three keepers tell the same local news (the Urchins robbed me last night) and each line ends on a crafted beat; Westwood's keepers rarely share one plot point.

items.label: B
items.critique: '[Person]'s the name, and iron's the trade!' and the wolves punchline are neatly built quips; every shop routes the player to the same threat, which reads designed rather than incidental.

items.label: C
items.critique: Flat, slogan-like 'Welcome to X! How can I help you?' and the shop-jingle 'one stop shop for all your literary needs' is exactly Nox's tongue-in-cheek blandness.

items.label: D
items.critique: Generic courteous greetings ('at your service! What can I do for you, sir [Class]?') with a small rival-inn aside; no plot exposition, typical of the campaign's shop lines.

items.label: E
items.critique: Each line stacks wares, local threat and a joke ('Well... the only ones, anyway!'); the precise geography ('east of the ford', 'from the barrow') in a shop greeting is a tell.

items.label: F
items.critique: Three variations on 'nobody comes since the bandits'; the triad 'Potions, scrolls and spell books' and the inviting rhetorical question are tidy but too uniformly themed.

items.label: G
items.critique: Ties into a chapter event but in Nox's boastful salesman way ('finest assortment of arms in the South!'), with a longer, slightly clumsy magic-shop line that feels authentic.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'fresher'n a monkey's butt' is Nox's crude humour; 'Welcome, Wanderer!' and the deadpan guarantee line are short and unpolished in the campaign's way.

items.label: I
items.critique: Every keeper explains an absence or emptiness with a wink ('there's nobody else in them!'); consistent three-beat joke construction across all three shops.

items.label: J
items.critique: Uneven register ('aye mate', 'Ya need', then a dry institutional sentence about the [Group]) is the inconsistency of the real campaign, not a designed voice.

tells: Westwood's shop greetings are short, generic and sales-slogan flat ('Welcome to X! How can I help you?'); the new ones always carry local plot news.
In the new texts all three keepers of a place share one topic (the same raiders or monster), which feels designed; Westwood's keepers are unrelated to each other.
New texts build each line to a punchline or tag joke; Westwood's humour is rarer, cruder and more random.
New texts give precise geography (east of the ford, north road) even in a shop greeting.
New texts favour the triad list 'Potions, scrolls and spell books' and the ' -- ' dash aside in nearly every line.
